chapterNote: The other cave psalm — Psalm 57's companion, but without its dawn. This one is a maskil, a psalm for teaching, and what it teaches is how to pray when you are at the bottom: aloud, with your whole voice, pouring out the complaint and telling God the trouble in detail, as if He did not know it. The loneliness is the sharpest in the Psalter: I look to my right, where a defender should stand, and no one recognizes me; refuge has perished from me; no one is asking after my soul. And then the turn, in the same breath: I cried to You, LORD; I said, You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living. The man who has lost every refuge names the one that is left. He is very low; the pursuers are stronger; so he asks to be brought out of the prison — the cave, the fear, the isolation — for one reason: that I may give thanks to Your name. The last picture is the loneliness reversed: the righteous will gather around me, crowning me, because You will have dealt generously with me. David in the cave, with four hundred distressed men about to find him (1 Samuel 22:2), praying for the company God would send.

1.text: A maskil of David, a prayer, when he was in the cave. With my voice I cry out to the LORD; with my voice I plead with the LORD for grace.
1.amp: Maschil ['A Psalm of David, giving instruction', maskil, the KJV margin] of David; A Prayer [tephillah] when he was in the cave [mearah]. I cried [zaaq — cried out for help] unto the LORD [YHWH] with my voice [qol]; with my voice unto the LORD did I make my supplication [chanan — plead for grace].
1.notes: maskil (H4905), a teaching psalm — and its lesson is prayer from a cave (mearah, H4631), Adullam or En-gedi, as in Psalm 57. qoli el-YHWH ezaq (H6963, H7121 area: zaaq H2199): OUT LOUD — zaaq is the alarm-cry — qoli el-YHWH etchannan (H2603): with my voice I beg for grace. The cave is where a man learns to pray audibly.

2.text: I pour out my complaint before Him; I tell Him my trouble face to face.
2.amp: I poured out [shaphak] my complaint [siach — musing, complaint] before [panim] Him; I showed [nagad — declared] before [panim] Him my trouble [tsarah].
2.notes: eshpokh le-phanav sichi (H8210, H6440, H7879): poured out — Hannah's verb — my siach, the murmured complaint; tsarati le-phanav aggid (H6869, H5046): my trouble DECLARED before Him, in detail, as if He needed the report. Prayer as full disclosure; God does not want the summary.

3.text: When my spirit fainted within me, You — You knew my path. On the road I walk they have hidden a trap for me.
3.amp: When my spirit [ruach] was overwhelmed [ataph — fainted, wrapped in weakness] within me, then You knew [yada] my path [netibah — trail]. In the way [orach] wherein [zu] I walked [halak] have they privily laid [taman — hidden, buried] a snare [pach] for me.
3.notes: be-hitateph alai ruchi (H5848, H7307): the fainting-wrap of Psalm 143:4 — ve-attah yadata netibati (H3045, H5410): and YOU knew my trail — the emphatic pronoun: when I could not see the path, You could. be-orach-zu ahallekh tamnu phach li (H734, H2098, H1980, H2934, H6341): a spring-trap buried on the very road he must walk.

4.text: Look to my right and see: there is no one who recognizes me. Every refuge has perished from me; no one is asking after my soul.
4.amp: I looked ['Look on the right hand, and see', nabat, the KJV margin] on my right hand [yamin], and beheld [raah], but there was no man that would know [nakar — recognize, acknowledge] me: refuge [manos] failed ['perished from me', abad, the KJV margin] me; no man cared ['sought after', darash, the KJV margin] for my soul [nephesh].
4.notes: habbet yamin u-reeh (H5027, H3225, H7200): look right — the side where a defender or advocate stood — ve-en-li makkir (H5234): no one recognizes me. abad manos mimmenni (H6, H4498): refuge has PERISHED from me; en doresh le-naphshi (H1875, H5315): no one is seeking after my soul — darash, the study-verb of Psalm 111:2, here for a person no one bothers to look into. The loneliest verse in the Psalter.

5.text: I cried out to You, O LORD, and I said, 'You are my shelter, my allotted portion in the land of the living.'
5.amp: I cried [zaaq] unto You, O LORD [YHWH]: I said [amar], You are my refuge [machseh — shelter] and my portion [cheleq — share, allotment] in the land [eretz] of the living [chay].
5.notes: zaaqti elekha YHWH (H2199): the same alarm-cry as verse 1, now with a confession inside it: attah machsi (H4268) — the manos that perished (v. 4) replaced by a machseh that cannot — chelqi be-eretz ha-chayyim (H2506, H776, H2416): my PORTION, the Levite's word for having God instead of land (cf. Numbers 18:20; Lamentations 3:24). A man with no inheritance names his inheritance.

6.text: Give attention to my ringing cry, for I have been brought very low; rescue me from those who pursue me, for they are stronger than I am.
6.amp: Attend [qashab — listen closely] unto my cry [rinnah — ringing cry]; for I am brought very [meod] low [dalal — hung low, brought down thin]: deliver [natsal] me from my persecutors [radaph — pursuers]; for they are stronger [amats] than I.
6.notes: haqshivah el-rinnati (H7181, H7440): rinnah is usually the ringing shout of joy; here it is the ringing cry of distress — ki-dalloti meod (H1809, H3966), Psalm 116:6's word, brought low and thin. hatsileni me-rodephai ki ametsu mimmenni (H5337, H7291, H553): Psalm 18:17's admission: they are stronger than I.

7.text: Bring my soul out of this prison, so that I may give thanks to Your name. The righteous will gather around me like a crown, because You will have dealt generously with me.
7.amp: Bring [yatsa] my soul [nephesh] out of prison [masger — the closed place, the dungeon], that I may praise [yadah] Your name [shem]: the righteous [tsaddiq] shall compass me about [kathar — surround, crown] me; for You shall deal bountifully [gamal — deal out fully] with me.
7.notes: hotsiah mi-masger naphshi (H3318, H4525, H5315): out of the masger, the shut place — the cave, and the isolation of verse 4 — le-hodot et-shemekha (H3034, H8034): the purpose is thanksgiving, as in Psalm 6:5. bi yakhtiru tsaddiqim (H3803, H6662): the righteous will kathar me — surround like a crown; the four hundred of Adullam (cf. 1 Samuel 22:2) arriving. ki tigmol alai (H1580): Psalm 13:6's gamal — the full dealing, expected before it comes.
